title: Byte's Bad Feeling
subtitle: The Library has a data type mystery
conceptSummary: Data types tell the database what KIND of data is in a column: TEXT, INTEGER, REAL (decimal), or DATE.

dialogue.text: We've got a tip from the City Library. Their system is acting weird when they search for books.
Probably a data type issue. Someone stored a year as TEXT instead of a number. Classic rookie mistake.
Which is why we have a rookie! Find all books published after 2000 — but first, understand the data types.

teachMoment.title: Data Types
teachMoment.body:
Every column has a type. Common ones:
• TEXT — words and sentences (always use quotes: 'Hello')
• INTEGER — whole numbers (42, 2024)
• REAL — decimal numbers (4.5, 199.99)
• DATE — stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD'

To filter, use WHERE:
SELECT * FROM books WHERE year_published > 2000

task.instruction: Find all books published AFTER the year 2000. Use WHERE to filter by year_published.
task.startingQuery:
SELECT title, author, year_published
FROM books
WHERE -- add your condition here
task.solution: SELECT title, author, year_published FROM books WHERE year_published > 2000

hints.text: 'After 2000' means year_published is greater than 2000. What symbol means 'greater than'?
Use > for 'greater than'. So: WHERE year_published > 2000
Full: SELECT title, author, year_published FROM books WHERE year_published > 2000

winDialogue.text: 7 books published after 2000. The library's search is fixed!
One of the loaned books has an interesting title: 'Data Science for Beginners'. Check who borrowed it.

storyBeat: A library member checked out a data science book and then vanished without returning it. The fine_amount is suspiciously zero. Someone tampered with the record.
